source_rules.shape: red candle; lower wick strictly below 0.2 times body; body strictly below 0.5 times the absolute full-sample signed mean body; upper wick at least twice body
source_rules.trend: star close no lower than prior close and prior close no lower than the close two bars earlier
source_rules.confirmation: following candle high no higher than star high and following candle close no higher than star close
source_rules.position: short at the star row, exit when a later close moves strictly beyond plus or minus 5 percent from star close or after seven workdays

defects_and_ambiguities: Conditions seven and eight read the following candle with a negative shift, but the source records the short signal on the earlier star row; this is direct lookahead.
The small-body threshold uses the signed mean of open minus close over the entire dataset, allowing future observations to alter every historical signal.
Taking the absolute value after averaging signed bodies permits bullish and bearish bodies to cancel, which is not a stable measure of typical body size.
The source enters at the star close even though confirmation is unknowable until the following close; a causal confirmed trade cannot earn the confirmation-bar return.
Overlapping stars accumulate positions without a gross-exposure limit, while independently scheduled exits can create unintended residual long or short positions.
The exit loop can run beyond the available frame for late signals and chained assignment can fail silently in modern pandas.
Raw OHLC is split-sensitive, while no spreads, turnover costs, borrow fees, uncertainty, controls, or out-of-sample windows are included.
independent_treatment: Do not report the biased source return. Replace its full-sample body statistic with a causal expanding statistic, delay confirmed entry until confirmation is complete, cap each asset and total gross exposure, prevent overlapping same-asset positions, and test both source-faithful signed-body and scale-normalized absolute-body interpretations. Also test the scale-normalized star without next-bar confirmation as a distinct predeclared candidate.
